questions: Does progress rise above the iteration 1 values (oval 0.11, s-bend 0.155, slalom 0.109) with the 2 cm lead?
Do line_loss_events fall to 0, or do they rise because the array now reads the bend later?
Is max_error still at or near 0.06 m, and at what progress does the run end?
Does steering_oscillation rise above about 0.15 with the shorter lead?
Does rms_error stay near 0.03 on all tracks, which would suggest a steady offset from the motor mismatch rather than a geometry limit?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If progress is unchanged and line losses are still 1 per run, tell me whether the sensor_size of 0.016 (larger footprint) or a ±4 cm span would help more. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.15, say whether the lead or the gains are the cause.

intent: Single-variable test from the best design (iteration 1): move the five-sensor array (±3 cm, 1.5 cm pitch, 12 mm footprints) from a 4 cm lead to a 2 cm lead to check whether a shorter lead reduces off-track exits. Keep all other geometry unchanged so the result isolates the lead. Expect progress above 0.15 on the s-bend and above 0.11 on the oval, max_error below 0.06 m, and line_loss_events at or near 0-1 per run. If the lead is not the limit, the next step is sensor_size 0.016 alone.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that widening to ±6 cm with 16 mm footprints removed line losses but did not stop the off-track exit, and it cut s-bend progress to 4%. So span and footprint are not the main limit. The lead is the remaining geometry variable, and it has not yet been tested below 3 cm. Measure progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on all three development tracks.
rationale: Race evidence so far. Iteration 0 (5 sensors, ±2 cm span, 5 cm lead, 0.8 kg) and iteration 1 (5 sensors, ±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track) both ended every run off track at 10-16% progress, with max_error at 0.061-0.066 m, which is the 0.06 m off-track limit. Iteration 1 reduced line losses from 1-2 to 1 per run and scored best (51.27). Iteration 2 widened to ±6 cm with 7 sensors, 16 mm footprints, a 3 cm lead and a 0.10 m track. Line losses fell to 0, but the score dropped to 26.99: s-bend progress fell to 4%, and the oval and slalom were unchanged at about 11% and 3.5%. So the wider, larger-footprint array did not fix the drift. Line losses now read 0 while the robot still exits at max_error of about 0.06 m, which means the sensors still see the tape and the robot leaves the line anyway. That points away from span and toward the lead or the balance between geometry and gains. The Integrator's request for a shorter lead when line losses are zero also fits this. Oscillation stayed low (0.065-0.155) in every iteration, so jitter is not the limit. I also see that rms_error stays near 0.03 in every design, which suggests a constant offset or drift that the geometry alone has not corrected. This iteration changes one variable from the best design (iteration 1): the lead moves from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.02 m. The span (±3 cm, 5 sensors, 12 mm footprints), mass (0.6 kg), track (0.11 m) and wheel radius (0.03 m) are kept, so any change in outcome can be attributed to the lead. Expected result: if the lead is the limit, progress on the s-bend and oval rises above the 0.15 and 0.11 seen so far, and max_error drops below 0.06 m. If progress falls or line losses rise, the lead is too close and the next step is to restore 0.04 m and test sensor_size 0.016 alone.
